asset_label: seismic or vibration time series from an accelerometer or geophone mounted on a bridge, building or other structure
source_note: Graded deterministically by cascade.signals.grade_signal, not by the image grader: each row carries a 'family' (which indicator it reads), 'min' (inclusive) and 'max' (exclusive) bounds on that indicator, and a 'source' tag. Indicators: frequency_shift_pct = |dominant frequency - baseline dominant frequency| / baseline * 100 per channel (worst channel used); pga_pct_g = peak absolute acceleration in percent of g (accelerometer with known units only); pgv_cm_s = peak absolute velocity in cm/s (geophone with known units only); rms_change_pct = (RMS - baseline RMS) / baseline RMS * 100. All thresholds and their status come from docs/research/10_multisensor_scope.md section 2.1: the ShakeMap instrumental-intensity table is [PUBLIC, secondary] (values attributed to USGS ShakeMap V4 / Worden et al. 2012 via search summary, R10 [16]; the note lists one PGA and one PGV per intensity class and this rubric reads each listed value as the lower edge of the class it labels [team-proposed, validate against the ShakeMap manual, which places the listed values at integer intensities]); every frequency-shift and RMS row is [team-proposed, validate] because the note found no universal published threshold ('Modal-frequency drop has no published universal threshold', R10 summary item 3; Salawu 1997 not verified, R10 [25]). The note's inference adopted here: 'a frequency-drop rule must be per-structure and temperature-compensated; do not put a single percentage on a slide', and 'All four map cleanly onto S0-S4 with U for no baseline'. No temperature compensation is implemented yet (open question R10 section 9 item 6).

rows.criterion: No stored baseline series for this asset: frequency shift and RMS change cannot be computed, so the structural condition is not assessable from this record. Grade U (never S0), collect a baseline under comparable excitation and temperature, and compare the next series against it. Source: R10 section 2.1 inference 'All four map cleanly onto S0-S4 with U for no baseline'.

|delta f| below 2 percent of the baseline dominant frequency. Not evidence of health: controlled-damage studies report drops 'ranging from 0.37% to 1.4%' (R10 [15], secondary), so small shifts sit inside this band; record and keep the baseline [team-proposed, validate]

|delta f| of 2 to 5 percent versus baseline. Below the tolerance one 2025 digital-twin paper uses to flag a measurement that 'deviates from the FEM-predicted value by more than a set tolerance (e.g. > 5 %)' (R10 [14], secondary); seasonal swings of this size can be normal, so compare against a same-season baseline before acting [team-proposed, validate]

|delta f| of 5 to 10 percent versus baseline: above the '> 5 %' model-deviation flag (R10 [14], secondary) but inside the band a crowdsourced-bridge paper warns about: 'large fluctuations, e.g., 5-10%, of a bridge's modal frequency can be normal in some climates' (R10 [14], secondary). Schedule a temperature-matched re-measurement and an inspection of the element [team-proposed, validate]

|delta f| of 10 percent or more versus baseline: beyond the 5-10 percent range that 'can be normal in some climates' (R10 [14], secondary); Z24 benchmark damage scenarios moved the second mode 'ranging from 5.02 to 4.72 Hz' (about 6 percent; R10 [20], secondary). Prioritize a structural review; check sensor mounting and baseline validity first [team-proposed, validate]
PGA below 6.2 %g: ShakeMap instrumental-intensity classes 'Not felt' (<0.0464 %g), 'Weak' (0.297) and 'Light' (2.76), no damage class listed (R10 [16], secondary)
rows.source: [PUBLIC, secondary] USGS ShakeMap V4 / Worden et al. 2012 via R10 [16]; band-edge reading [team-proposed, validate]

rows.criterion: PGA 6.2 to 11.5 %g: ShakeMap class 6.2 'Moderate / Very light damage' (R10 [16], secondary)
PGA 11.5 to 21.5 %g: ShakeMap class 11.5 'Strong / Light' damage (R10 [16], secondary)
PGA 21.5 to 40.1 %g: ShakeMap class 21.5 'Very strong / Moderate' damage (R10 [16], secondary)
PGA 40.1 %g or more: ShakeMap classes 40.1 'Severe / Moderate-heavy', 74.7 'Violent / Heavy', >139 'Extreme / Very heavy' damage (R10 [16], secondary)
PGV below 4.65 cm/s: ShakeMap classes 'Not felt' (<0.0215 cm/s), 'Weak' (0.135) and 'Light' (1.41), no damage class listed (R10 [16], secondary)
PGV 4.65 to 9.64 cm/s: ShakeMap class 4.65 'Moderate / Very light damage' (R10 [16], secondary)
PGV 9.64 to 20 cm/s: ShakeMap class 9.64 'Strong / Light' damage (R10 [16], secondary)
PGV 20 to 41.4 cm/s: ShakeMap class 20 'Very strong / Moderate' damage (R10 [16], secondary)
PGV 41.4 cm/s or more: ShakeMap classes 41.4 'Severe / Moderate-heavy', 85.8 'Violent / Heavy', >178 'Extreme / Very heavy' damage (R10 [16], secondary)

RMS below 1.5 times the baseline RMS (increase under 50 percent, or any decrease). No published RMS threshold was found in R10; RMS tracks excitation level (traffic, wind) as much as condition, so this family only records [team-proposed, validate]
RMS 1.5 to 3 times the baseline RMS. Check excitation and sensor gain before reading it as condition change [team-proposed, validate]
RMS 3 times the baseline RMS or more. Schedule a site check of sensor and structure; this family never escalates on its own [team-proposed, validate]

unified_note: The finding takes the worst level over the families that could be evaluated; families that could not (no baseline, unknown units, wrong sensor type) add the flag not_measurable and are listed in the justification. If no family can be evaluated the finding is U. PGA and PGV describe site shaking, not the structure: a strong event with a clean frequency comparison stays at the PGA/PGV level and tells the reviewer to look, it does not prove damage. Damping ratio (log decrement) is reported as an indicator only: the statistical thresholds in R10 [13] ('around 1 sigma' to 'beyond 6 sigma') need a population of baseline windows this module does not yet hold.

flags.not_measurable: set when a family could not be evaluated (no baseline, unknown units, sensor type without PGA/PGV)
